safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear". (غرقا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, since it meets it in meaning [Note: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "النازع is the one who pulls deeply (al-mughriq) when drawing the arrow or the soul; it is a maṣdar with the augment deleted, i.e. إغراقا. It is also permissible that it be a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. 'possessors of deep pulling'."]. (الواو) is a conjunction in both places, and likewise (الفاء) in both places. (أمرا) a direct object of the active participle on المدبّرات.
Clause: « (أقسم) بالنازعات ... » has no grammatical position; it is an initial clause ... and the answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being "you will surely be resurrected, O disbelievers".

* Morphology:
(النازعات): plural of النازعة, feminine of النازع, an active participle from the triliteral نزع; its wazn is فاعل; النازعات are the angels.
(الناشطات): plural of الناشطة, feminine of الناشط, an active participle from the triliteral نشط; its wazn is فاعل; الناشطات are the angels.
(السابحات): plural of السابحة, feminine of السابح, an active participle from the triliteral سبح; its wazn is فاعل; السابحات are the angels.
(السابقات): plural of السابقة, feminine of السابق, an active participle from the triliteral سبق; its wazn is فاعل; السابقات are the angels.
(المدبّرات): plural of المدبّرة, feminine of المدبّر, an active participle from the quadriliteral دبّر; its wazn is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(غرقا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb غرق, bāb naṣara; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn..
Or it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of (أغرق).
(نشطا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb نشط, bāb ḍaraba; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn..
(سبقا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb سبق, bāb ḍaraba; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn..

safi-cedvel:6-11.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to the verb implied in لتبعثنّ. (قلوب) a mubtadaʾ, nominative, whose khabar is the clause أبصارها خاشعة. (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative – or indeclinable on fatḥa because it is annexed to the indeclinable إذ – attached to (واجفة) [Note: or it is a badal from يوم ترجف]. (واجفة) an adjective of قلوب [Note: separating the adjective from the described noun by an intervening element was permissible because it is an adverb], nominative. (أبصارها) a second mubtadaʾ, nominative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the eyes of their owners".. its khabar is (خاشعة)..
Clause: «ترجف الراجفة ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «تتبعها الرادفة ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from الراجفة.
And the clause: «قلوب ... أبصارها خاشعة» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «أبصارها خاشعة» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (قلوب).
10- 11 (الهمزة) for interrogation of denial. (اللام) for emphasis, and it is the shifted lām (al-muzaḥlaqa). (في الحافرة) attached to (مردودون). (الهمزة) like the first. (إذا) an indeclinable adverb in the position of accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis..
And the clause: «يقولون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" (they)..
And the nominal clause is a ḥāl from the possessors of the throbbing hearts [Note: It is permissible that the clause يقولون be an explanatory resumption].
And the clause: «إنّا لمردودون ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «كنّا عظاما ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then shall we be raised anew?".

* Morphology:
(6) الراجفة: feminine of الراجف, an active participle from the triliteral رجف; its wazn is فاعل.
(7) الرادفة: feminine of الرادف, an active participle from the triliteral ردف; its wazn is فاعل.
(8) واجفة: feminine of واجف, an active participle from the triliteral وجف; its wazn is فاعل.
(10) الحافرة: a name for the road on which a person returns by the way he came, and by it the return in conditions from the end of the matter to its beginning is expressed.. It is on the wazn فاعل in the sense of مفعول, and what is meant by it here is the earth.
(11) نخرة: feminine of نخر, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral نخر al-ʿaẓm, bāb fariḥa, when it has decayed; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then kasra.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in the saying of the Exalted «يوم ترجف الراجفة».
The attribution to it is figurative, because it is the cause of the quaking.

* Benefits:
- Deletion of the answer to the oath:
It is obligatory to delete it if something that indicates the answer precedes it or surrounds it, as in (زيد قائم والله) ("Zayd is standing, by Allah").
And from it: (إن جاءني زيد والله أكرمته) ("If Zayd comes to me, by Allah, I will honour him"). These are examples in which the answer precedes and so is deleted. Likewise the answer is deleted if something indicating the answer surrounds it, such as: «زيد والله قائم». If you say: (زيد والله إنه قائم), it is possible that the later part is a khabar for the earlier, and it is possible that it is the answer, the clause of the oath and its answer being the khabar. It is permissible in other cases as well, as in the saying of the Exalted in the sūra we are dealing with: (وَالنَّازِعاتِ غَرْقاً. وَالنَّاشِطاتِ نَشْطاً); the answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being (لتبعثن), as shown by what follows; and this implied element is the operator in the saying of the Exalted (يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ), or its operator is the omitted (اذكر) ("remember"). Like it is (ق وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ), where the answer is implied as (ليهلكن), as shown by (كَمْ أَهْلَكْنا). And like it is (ص وَالْقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ), i.e. (إنه لمعجز).

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(إذا) with tanwīn – a particle of response, with no grammatical position [Note: إذا – with tanwīn – expresses an implied condition, i.e.: "if we are returned to the ḥāfira and that is true, then it is a losing return"].
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption confirming the preceding clause يقولون.
And the clause: «تلك ... كرّة ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(خاسرة): feminine of خاسر, an active participle from the triliteral خسر, bāb fariḥa; its wazn is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in the saying of the Exalted «تِلْكَ إِذاً كَرَّةٌ خاسِرَةٌ».
Loss is attributed to the return, while what is meant is its owners. The meaning: if our return to the Resurrection is true, then that return is a losing return.

safi-cedvel:13-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive. (إنّما) the restraining and the restrained [kāffa and makfūfa]. (الفاء) the second links to the apodosis of an implied condition. (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya). (بالساهرة) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). Clause: «هي زجرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or it is a reason for something implied, said by an implied "say", i.e. the Exalted said: That is not hard, because it is a single cry].
And the clause: «هم بالساهرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "when the Trumpet is blown, then behold they ...".

* Morphology:
(13) زجرة: a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar marra) from the triliteral زجر; its wazn is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.
(واحدة): feminine of واحد, the name of the first of the arithmetical numbers; its wazn is فاعل.
(14) الساهرة: feminine of الساهر, an adjective of the earth or the open desert because whoever traverses it does not sleep out of fear; its wazn is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:15-26.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) an interrogative particle. (إذ) an adverb of past time in the position of accusative, attached to (حديث). (بالواد) attached to a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (ناداه) [Note: or attached to (ناداه)], and the sign of genitive is the kasra implied on the deleted yāʾ, because of the reading in connected speech (waṣl) owing to the meeting of two sākin letters. (طوى) ʿaṭf bayān to الوادي – or a badal from it – genitive..
Clause: «أتاك حديث ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «ناداه ربّه ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «اذهب ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «إنّه طغى ... » has no grammatical position; it is a causal clause.
And the clause: «طغى ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
18- 19 (الفاء) conjunction. (هل) an interrogative particle. (لك) a fronted khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "an inclination" or "a way". (أن) a maṣdar particle governing the accusative.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تزكّى) is in the position of genitive by (إلى), attached to the implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "an inclination to purify yourself".
(الواو) conjunction. (أهديك) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (تزكّى). (إلى ربّك) attached to (أهديك) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "to knowledge of your Lord". (الفاء) causal. (تخشى) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif, and the fāʿil is "you".
And the clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اذهب.
And the clause: «هل لك (ميل ... ) » is in the position of accusative, the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «تزكّى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «أهديك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تزكّى.
And the clause: «تخشى ... » has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the knowledge.
20- 26 (الفاء) is a conjunction in the five places. (الآية) a second object, accusative. (الواو, ثمّ) two conjunctions. (نكال) a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar of an omitted verb [Note: it is a noun of the maṣdar, i.e. "He made an example of him (nakkala bihi) nakāl".. It may also stand in for the maṣdar because its verb meets it in meaning, so "Allah seized him" is a nakāl.. It is also permissible that it be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi]. (الآخرة) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive – and it is an adjective of an omitted described noun, i.e. "the last word" – and likewise الأولى. (في ذلك) attached to the khabar of إنّ. (اللام) for emphasis. (لمن) attached to an adjective of (عبرة)..
And the clause: «أراه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so he went to Pharaoh and showed him".
And the clause: «كذّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أراه.
And the clause: «عصى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّب.
And the clause: «أدبر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّب.
And the clause: «يسعى ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of أدبر.
And the clause: «حشر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أدبر.
And the clause: «نادى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause حشر.
And the clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نادى.
And the clause: «أنا ربّكم ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «أخذه الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال.
And the clause: «إنّ في ذلك لعبرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the seizing [Note: Some exegetes made this clause the answer to the oath with which the sūra began..].
And the clause: «يخشى» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(16) الواد: it is written in the muṣḥaf without yāʾ, in observance of its deletion in recitation because of the meeting of two sākin letters.
(18) تزكّى: an imperfect from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted.. What is mentioned in Sūrat Ṭāhā is a past verb, in which the yāʾ is changed into alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa.
(20) أراه: the first hamza is one of the augment letters in the verb, so it is the hamza of أفعل, and the alif before the hāʾ is the lām of the verb; as for its ʿayn – the hamza, the bare form being رأى – it has been deleted for lightening after transferring its vowel to the rāʾ; the original is أرآه (أرأاه) – with a hamza and then an alif after it – its wazn is أفله [Note: see also verse (55) of Sūrat al-Baqara].
(24) الأعلى: on the pattern of the elative noun, but the elative is not intended by it, rather the description; its wazn is أفعل, and the lām of the word is changed from a yāʾ – being fourth – and its original is a wāw from العلوّ.. the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.

safi-cedvel:27-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation of rebuke. (خلقا) a tamyīz, accusative. (السماء) conjoined to the pronoun mubtadaʾ (أنتم) by the conjunction, and the fāʿil of (بناها) is a pronoun referring to Allah, understood from the context ...
Clause: «أنتم أشدّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «بناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «رفع ... » has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «سوّاها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رفع.
And the clause: «أغطش ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رفع.
And the clause: «أخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رفع.

* Morphology:
(أشدّ): an elative from the triliteral شدّ; its wazn is أفعل, and its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.
(خلقا): a maṣdar of the triliteral خلق; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(سمكها): a maṣdar of سمك, i.e. "became thick and dense".. its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(سوّاها): it contains an iʿlāl by substitution, whose analogy is like (بناها): the yāʾ – the lām of the word – was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(ضحاها): a name for the time between the sun's rising and noon; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then fatḥa..
And see verse (98) of al-Aʿrāf.

safi-cedvel:30-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (الأرض) a direct object of an omitted verb by way of occupation (ishtighāl), which is explained by what follows, i.e. دحى.. (بعد) an adverb, accusative, attached to the implied (دحى). (منها) attached to (أخرج). (الجبال) like الأرض, i.e. "He fixed the mountains". (متاعا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. "He gave you enjoyment by that, an enjoyment" [Note: It is permissible that it be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi whose operator is omitted, i.e. "He did that as an enjoyment ..."], so it stands in for the maṣdar because it meets it in derivation. (لكم) attached to (متاعا), and likewise لأنعامكم, which is conjoined to it.
Clause: « (دحى) الأرض ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «دحاها» has no grammatical position; it is explicative (tafsīriyya).
And the clause: «أخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: « (أرسى) الجبال ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause (دحى) الأرض [Note: It may be parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) if the operator of (متاعا) is the verb أخرج].
And the clause: «أرساها ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.

* Morphology:
(30) دحاها: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution like سوّاها [Note: in verse (27) of the sūra]; the alif originates from a wāw or a yāʾ.
(31) مرعاها: originally a noun of place, then used as a majāz mursal for trees, herbage and what a person eats.. it contains an iʿlāl by substitution: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.. its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn.
(32) أرساها: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution; the alif originates from a yāʾ in the augmented form, and from a wāw in the bare form; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal: in the saying of the Exalted «أَخْرَجَ مِنْها ماءَها وَمَرْعاها».
Here المرعى is used for anything eaten, by man and others. It may also be an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), because the discourse is with the deniers of the Gathering, as attested by «أَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً». It is as though it were said: O you obstinate ones who are paired with the beasts in enjoying this world and being oblivious of the Hereafter.

safi-cedvel:34-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive. (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "he is reckoned" [Note: It is permissible that it be a badal from (إذا), and so be attached to the apodosis]. (ما) a maṣdar particle. (لمن) attached to (برّزت).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما سعى) is in the position of accusative, a direct object.
Clause: «جاءت الطامّة ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis is implied, i.e. "people are resurrected".
And the clause: «يتذكّر الإنسان ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi..
And the clause: «سعى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
And the clause: «برّزت الجحيم ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يتذكّر.
And the clause: «يرى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(34) الطامّة: a name for the calamity; it came on the pattern of the active participle of the triliteral طمّ, i.e. "rose high and overcame"; the tāʾ is redundant for intensification like the tāʾ of الداهية; its wazn is فاعلة, and its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.

safi-cedvel:37-41.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction of ramification (tafrīʿ). (أمّا) a non-jussive-governing conditional particle. (من) a relative in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "is punished". (الفاء) the second is causal. (هي) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl)..
Clause: «من طغى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause [Note: in verse (34) of the sūra, which is composed of the condition, its verb and its apodosis].
And the clause: «طغى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «آثر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause طغى.
And the clause: «إنّ الجحيم ... المأوى» has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the omitted khabar..
And the apodosis is implied, indicated by the khabar.
40- 41 (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (أمّا من خاف ... ) like أمّا من طغى [Note: in verse (37) of this sūra]. (عن الهوى) attached to (نهى). (الفاء) causal. (إنّ الجنّة هي المأوى) like إنّ الجحيم هي المأوى [Note: in the preceding verse (39)].
And the clause: «من خاف ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من طغى.
And the clause: «نهى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خاف, the ṣila of من.
And the clause: «إنّ الجنّة ... المأوى» has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the omitted khabar..
And the apodosis is implied, indicated by the khabar, namely: "he enters Paradise".

* Morphology:
(37) طغى: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution; its original is طغي, its maṣdar طغيان; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(آثر): the madda is composed of two hamzas, the first with fatḥa and the second sākin (أأثر); its wazn is أفعل, its imperfect يؤثر like أكرم يكرم.
(39) المأوى: a noun of place from the triliteral أوى; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn; it is a lafīf maqrūn (a verb with two weak letters adjacent).

* Rhetoric:
The art of muqābala (antithetical correspondence): in these noble verses, where several antitheses (ṭibāq) occur; and the multiplicity of ṭibāq, as is well known in the science of rhetoric, is called muqābala.

safi-cedvel:42-46.t:
* I'rab:
(عن الساعة) attached to (يسألونك). (أيّان) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, an adverb of time, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (مرساها). (فيم) a preposition and an interrogative noun in the position of genitive, attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنت. (من ذكراها) attached to the implied khabar. (إلى ربّك) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (منتهاها) ..
Clause: «يسألونك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «أيّان مرساها ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «فيم أنت ... » has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «إلى ربّك منتهاها ... » has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the interrogative that includes the meaning of denial.
45- 46 (إنّما) the restraining and the restrained [kāffa and makfūfa]. (من) a relative in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi. (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of the negated (يلبثوا). (إلّا) for restriction. (عشيّة) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يلبثوا). (أو) a conjunction.. (ضحاها) conjoined to عشيّة [Note: The annexation of الضحا to the pronoun of العشيّة is because they belong to one day; the connection between them permits the annexation of one to the other].
And the clause: «أنت منذر ... » has no grammatical position; it is another reason.
And the clause: «يخشاها ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «كأنّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يرونها ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «لم يلبثوا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of كأنّ.

* Morphology:
(عشيّة): a noun meaning the evening; its wazn is فعيلة, and the yāʾ of فعيلة and the lām of the word are of one letter.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of the Exalted «أَيَّانَ مُرْساها».
There is an explicit metaphor in the discourse, where "mooring" (irsāʾ) is borrowed, though it is used only for what has weight.
